Panel marca peers compartidos como Connected aunque no usen la VPN (status.go usa Online en vez de Active)
bugs.description: El panel de Ultron AP muestra como "Connected" a peers de Tailscale que en realidad no están utilizando la VPN. El problema es especialmente visible con dispositivos compartidos desde otro tailnet (ShareeNode: true). Caso real: usuario XIMENA GONZALEZ (ximenagonzalez0001@gmail.com), IP 100.85.52.11, mostrado como "Connected" pese a que el dispositivo no estaba conectado. Causa raíz: en internal/tailscale/status.go:78 se asigna Online: p.Online directamente desde la respuesta de Tailscale. El campo Online de Tailscale significa "el demonio del peer está vivo y registrado en el control plane", no "el túnel está siendo usado". Tailscale ya expone el dato correcto en el mismo JSON: el campo Active indica si el túnel está realmente en uso. Componente: internal/tailscale/status.go. Fix propuesto (Opción A, mínima): añadir Active bool `json:"Active"` al struct rawPeer (líneas 34–41) y cambiar Online: p.Online por Online: p.Active en el bucle que construye los peers (líneas 71–81), o renombrar Peer.Online → Peer.Active y propagar a la plantilla web. Opción B (más completa): mantener ambos campos en Peer (Online = demonio vivo, Active = túnel en uso) y dejar que la UI elija. Notas: verificar también el manejo de LastSeen zero-value (0001-01-01T00:00:00Z) — tratarlo como "nunca visto" y renderizar "—".
steps_to_reproduce: Compartir un dispositivo desde otro tailnet hacia el tailnet de Ultron (ShareeNode: true).
Apagar o desconectar el dispositivo compartido para que no esté usando la VPN.
Abrir el panel de Ultron AP y observar el estado del peer.
Comparar con la salida de `tailscale status --json` para ese peer.
bugs.expected_result: El indicador "Connected" del panel debe reflejar uso real del túnel, no solo el estado del demonio remoto. Si el peer no está activo (Active=false) y/o no tiene handshake reciente, el panel debe mostrarlo como No conectado. Solo si Active=true (o hay tráfico/handshake reciente) debe mostrarse como Conectado.
bugs.actual_result: El panel muestra el peer como "Connected" porque status.go usa el campo Online de Tailscale, que solo indica que el demonio remoto está vivo en el control plane. El peer aparece conectado aunque Active=false, LastHandshake/LastSeen/LastWrite estén en valor cero, RxBytes=TxBytes=0 e InEngine=false.
bugs.evidence: tailscale status --json para el peer afectado: { "HostName": "device-of-shared-to-user", "Online": true, "Active": false, "LastSeen": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z", "LastHandshake": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z", "LastWrite": "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z", "RxBytes": 0, "TxBytes": 0, "InEngine": false, "ShareeNode": true }

bugs.title: Alert rule rule_id=11 flaps between fire and resolve every 15-20 min (no hysteresis / for-duration)
steps_to_reproduce: Run the alert engine (interval=5s) with rule_id=11 (resource, cause_source=proc) and observe the journal across several hours
bugs.expected_result: A fire only when the threshold breach is sustained for a configurable for_duration (e.g. 60-120s); resolve only after the condition stays clear for resolve_for_duration; optional cooldown before the next fire
bugs.actual_result: Engine evaluates the threshold every 5s and emits fire/resolve immediately on each crossing. Cycles fire→resolve last 3-30s and repeat every 15-20 min, generating spurious alerts and notification noise

bugs.title: Settings alert widgets dead when navigating via sidebar (hx-boost doesn't reload head)
bugs.description: Scoped to FR-058 widget script loading. Network alert rules UI/engine (FR-022) gap split out to BG-039.
steps_to_reproduce: Open any non-settings page (e.g. /dashboard)
Click 'Settings' in the sidebar (hx-boost link)
Scroll to Alert rules section
Click any severity segmented button, cooldown chip preset, or +/− stepper
Observe: nothing happens
bugs.expected_result: Segmented severity click updates hidden <input name=severity>; chip preset populates cooldown field; stepper increments/decrements value; POST carries the chosen values — regardless of how the user got to /settings (direct URL, hard refresh, or hx-boost sidebar navigation).
bugs.actual_result: Widget scripts in base.html <head> are gated by {{if eq .ActivePage "settings"}}. hx-boost swaps the body but NOT the head, so when users navigate to /settings from any other page via the sidebar, the widget JS never loads. Widgets render correct HTML (data-widget=segmented/chip-preset/stepper) but have no click handlers attached. Direct URL load / hard refresh works correctly. The form submits with default/empty values, making alert customization impossible.
bugs.environment: local — settings-revamp + network-monitoring features, both marked verify ✅ in pipeline

bugs.title: FR-022 network alert rules: engine + UI never implemented
steps_to_reproduce: Open /settings → Alert rules → click Metric select
Look for: latency / loss / dns_failure / wan_outage / public_ip_change
Open /network and look for an alert-rule creation tab/section
bugs.expected_result: Metric select includes network metric types (FR-022). Settings (or /network) exposes UI to create network rules with sustained-duration parameter (BG-037 hysteresis is part of this). Alert engine evaluates these rule types and fires via existing notification channels.
bugs.actual_result: isValidMetric() in internal/server/handlers_settings.go only accepts cpu/ram/disk/temp. Alert engine in internal/alerts/engine.go has zero references to latency/loss/dns/wan/public_ip. network.html has no alert-rule UI. The acceptance criterion 'Network rules render in the existing alerts panel ... mutable from the same settings UI patterns' is unmet. This is a substantial implementation gap and should be routed via aitri feature init network-alerts (or fr-change), not a maintenance-path bug-fix.
bugs.environment: Pi 192.168.1.29 / production / pipeline marked verify ✅ but FR-022 partially implemented
bugs.evidence: internal/server/handlers_settings.go:82-88, internal/alerts/engine.go (no network metric handling), web/templates/network.html (no rule UI), spec/BUGS.json BG-038 (split source)

bugs.title: Unclean shutdown: SSE connections never close, so httpServer.Shutdown always times out and systemd marks the service failed on every restart
steps_to_reproduce: systemctl restart ultron-ap while a dashboard tab is open
bugs.actual_result: 'Server forced to shutdown: context deadline exceeded' after 10s, exit code 1, 'ultron-ap.service: Failed with result exit-code'. httpServer.Shutdown waits for active connections; the SSE handler loops until the CLIENT disconnects, so it never returns. Restarts also take 10s longer than they should.

bugs.title: Sidebar broken after hx-boost navigation: logo stretches (39x76) and the collapsed state is lost, the toggle stops resizing
steps_to_reproduce: Collapse the sidebar, then navigate with a sidebar link
bugs.expected_result: The sidebar stays collapsed and the logo stays square (40x40)
bugs.actual_result: The logo renders 39x76 (stretched) because the collapse rules live in @layer components and Tailwind v4's utilities layer always wins over components regardless of specificity — the h-[76px] utility overrides them. After a boost swap the sidebar comes back with the server's classes (sidebar-hidden) and no one reapplies the stored state, so the collapse is lost and the toggle no longer resizes.
bugs.resolution: Fixed, browser-verified across five navigation steps.

bugs.title: Sidebar collapse button unreachable: min-h-screen stretches the aside to the full page height (1486px), pushing the button below the viewport
steps_to_reproduce: Open the dashboard on a 900px-tall screen and look for the collapse button
bugs.expected_result: The button sits at the bottom of the sidebar, on screen
bugs.actual_result: The body is a flex row, so min-h-screen makes the aside stretch to the tallest child (the dashboard content, 1486px). The button lands at y=1450 — below the fold — and sticky does nothing because the element already spans the whole page. The sidebar cannot be collapsed without scrolling to the very bottom.
bugs.resolution: Fixed and browser-verified with real mouse clicks.
